sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
claims: The official English name is Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. (SBIC East Japan).
Corporate number is 9011001030621; headquarters are in Shibuya, Tokyo.
The company was established on 1963-11-15 and reports capital of JPY 6,673,400,000.

Its shareholders are described by category as local governments (18 prefectures), chambers of commerce, financial institutions and operating companies; individual shareholder names are not enumerated on this profile page.
Nagoya Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. and Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. are identified as sister companies.
limitations: The profile does not identify SBI Holdings as a parent or subsidiary; the shareholder categories are not a named shareholder register.
This profile does not establish any XRP, Ripple, Coinbase or Circle investment, custody, payment or partnership relationship.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
claims: The company describes the SME investment-development system as a national SME policy and itself as a policy implementation institution.
It states that it was initially established with some government capital but is now a private corporation conducting independent investment activity.
It states that it is not a government financial institution and operates under the Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Company Act, Act No. 101 of 1963.
It describes its role as a long-term stable shareholder supporting SME equity capital and growth, without management interference or dispatching directors.
limitations: The policy-implementation role must not be simplified into current government ownership or government-bank status.
No cryptoasset or XRP mandate is established by this material.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
claims: A two-day introductory generative-AI and machine-learning course ran June 12-13, 2025.
The curriculum explicitly included how to use ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, prompt application, code generation and information-leakage risk.
The course was restricted to SBIC investee companies; the listed investee-company fee was JPY 35,000 and general companies were not eligible.
The named instructor was from VOST, not OpenAI.
limitations: A training topic or course does not establish an OpenAI partnership, API agreement, model deployment or XRP relationship.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
claims: SBIC published a February 26, 2025 seminar titled 'The Present and Future of Generative AI (ChatGPT)'.
The announcement says the event was co-hosted with the Tokyo Chamber of Commerce and Industry's Taito branch.
The named speaker was a Microsoft representative; the event was free with a stated capacity of 130.
limitations: The announcement establishes an educational event, not an OpenAI commercial partnership or an XRP connection.

claims: SBI Holdings' May 21, 2007 release identifies SBI CAPITAL Co., Ltd. as its buy-out and enterprise-revitalization funds-management unit.
The release says SBI transferred 40% of SBI CAPITAL to Jupiter Investment Y.K., described as a Goldman Sachs group company, effective May 23, 2007.
The post-transfer ownership ratio was 60% SBI Holdings and 40% Jupiter Investment Y.K.
The historical SBI CAPITAL entity and its SBIC funds are distinct from Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. (SBIC East Japan).
limitations: This is a historical 2007 ownership snapshot, not evidence of the current legal status or current ownership of SBI Capital.
A shared acronym is not evidence that the historical SBI CAPITAL and SBIC East Japan are the same legal entity.
